I tested this on my end. Having up to 12 instantiated scenes works fine, from 13+ it crashes on startup. First I thought it might be because all animations are working on the same property (:position:y), but this doesn't seem to matter. 

I am currently investigating further

Edit: ~~I did some print-debugging and when adding 13 scenes the _ready() prints don't even happen. So it crashes even before adding any animations to the animationlibrary.

Maybe it's the simple fact that >12 animationplayers try to get assigned the same animationlibrary~~

Edit2: Further testing suggests that actually calling the play("global/<name>") seems to provoke the crash.

I've narrowed it down to crash here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ef34c3d534a16b140aef0643ed2fa36f8e9d1612/scene/animation/animation_player.cpp#L308

But only when having >= 13 animationplayers / animations (still need to differentiate). 

Edit: Upon further investigation the animationplayer itself is not necessarily the issue here.
I used fewer animationplayers but repeatedly added animations via code and the limiting factor here seems to be the animations in the animationlibrary (be it how many are added at once or anything else.... this requires further testing).

I've found that it happens because `playback.current.from->animation` pointer is invalid after adding too many animations to the same animationlibrary.

A minimal reproduction project would be helpful to confirm the issue and get a useful stacktrace with debug symbols.

I tried with the code snippet in the OP and couldn't get a crash on Linux in the current `master` branch, also when running it in a `for i in 50` loop.

[anim-bug-test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23583536/anim-bug-test.zip)
